title: 1812 and 1835: grapevines, dead trees and fallen logs by the river
items: Riverbank grape hangs in curtains over the water side of the river's edge trees, with its green July fruit, and Virginia creeper climbs the shaded side of their trunks.
Some trees in the river woods and the wet woods now stand dead and grey, and fallen trunks lie on the ground beside them.
The vines follow the riverbank records; how many trees are dead or down is reconstructed under a new liberty.
